exact_semantics_role: L2_EXACT_SEMANTICS remains a required soundness condition, not a failed obligation. The barrier says this fixed FPC model cannot be both universally total (L1) and exact (L2) on the affine subclass; it may remain L2-sound by returning OPEN/no decision on instances it cannot express.

fixed_global_transition_model.name: UNORDERED_FIXED_POINT_LOGIC_WITH_COUNTING_GLOBAL_DECISION
fixed_global_transition_model.semantics: The decision/progress invariant is required to be definable uniformly in fixed-point logic with counting over the unordered relational encoding of the constraint instance, without an externally supplied linear order or rank operator.
fixed_global_transition_model.why_global: FPC permits global fixed-point iteration and counting and is strictly richer than bounded-local Datalog.

published_theorem.title: Affine systems of equations and counting infinitary logic
published_theorem.statement_used: Testing solvability of systems of equations over a fixed finite Abelian group is not definable in the infinitary logic with finitely many variables and counting; consequently it is not definable in least fixed-point logic or its extension with counting on the unordered relational encodings considered.
published_theorem.tractability_fact: The affine CSP is polynomial-time decidable; over GF(2), Gaussian elimination gives an exact polynomial-time solver.

derived_TRUMP_barrier.claim: An unordered FPC-only route cannot provide universal exact exit even for the affine/GF(2) tractable subclass.
reason: The cited theorem shows that total affine solvability is not definable in the fixed FPC/counting language.
Thus a sound FPC mechanism may remain partial/OPEN, but it cannot discharge L1 while preserving L2 exactness on the whole affine subclass.
TRUMP's exact GF(2) route uses algebraic/rank information not captured by this fixed FPC model.

dead_zone_mapping.meaning: The correct sound response to an unexpressible case is OPEN/no decision, not an incorrect SAT/UNSAT verdict.

what_is_not_proved: L2 exact semantics is not refuted for partial FPC outputs.
No lower bound is claimed for algorithms using concrete input order/variable indices.
No lower bound is claimed for rank-extended fixed-point logics.
No runtime lower bound is claimed for arbitrary polynomial-time algorithms.

TRUMP_architecture_consequence.rule: A future global implicit language must preserve the exact affine/GF(2) capability; otherwise it can remain a sound partial observer but cannot become a universal decision layer.

next_admissible_math.question: Can a stronger global implicit language with rank/linear-algebra operators restore affine totality while preserving polynomial evaluation, and what theorem boundary applies to that stronger fixed model?
